executive_summary.headline: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 claims the first open 3T-class model, with full weights still pending
executive_summary.body: Kimi K3 launched July 14 as a 2.8T-parameter open MoE model with a 1M-token context window and native vision, available now on Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API at $3.00/M input (cache miss) and $15.00/M output. The catch: full open weights are promised only by July 27 — a week after this brief's window closes — so the 'open' claim is not yet independently verifiable and should be tracked, not acted on.

executive_summary.headline: Fireworks AI's $1.5B round at $17.5B is the clearest inference-infrastructure signal of the week
executive_summary.body: Fireworks closed a $1.505B Series D on July 16 at a $17.5B post-money valuation — roughly 4x its October mark — led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures, and TCV, with Nvidia participating. Annualized revenue passed $1B, up 5x year-over-year, evidence that enterprise demand for cheaper, customized model serving (versus frontier-API-only strategies) is accelerating.

executive_summary.headline: Anthropic pushes Claude Cowork from desktop-only to phone and browser
executive_summary.body: Cowork, Anthropic's background-agent feature, is expanding via beta from the desktop app to iPhone, iPad, Android, and claude.ai starting the week of July 13, with a gradual rollout beginning on the Max plan. Anthropic is extending doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5 to cover the transition — a low-risk moment to pilot cross-device agent handoff for knowledge-work tasks.

executive_summary.headline: xAI shipped two product moves in one week: open-sourced Grok Build, launched Automations
executive_summary.body: Following a privacy scandal over uploading users' private repos, xAI open-sourced the ~844,530-line Grok Build codebase under Apache 2.0 on July 15-16. Separately, on July 16 xAI shipped Grok Automations — natural-language scheduled and email-triggered agent tasks on grok.com and the iOS/Android apps, with email triggers gated to SuperGrok subscribers.

executive_summary.headline: Industrial-relevant funding: InstaLILY's Series B pulls in Home Depot Ventures and United Rentals
executive_summary.body: InstaLILY, which builds AI 'engineers' for physical-goods distributors and field-service workflows, closed a $60M Series B on July 14 led by Energize Capital, with Insight Partners increasing its stake and Home Depot Ventures and United Rentals joining as new strategic investors — a direct signal of enterprise AI investment converging on building-products and industrial distribution use cases.

top_picks.title: Kimi K3 Launches as First Open 3T-Class Model — Full Weights Pending
top_picks.summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3, a 2.8T-parameter open mixture-of-experts model with native vision and a 1M-token context window, calling it the world's first open 3T-class model. It's live now on Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API (model id kimi-k3) at $3.00/M input (cache miss), $0.30/M (cache hit), and $15.00/M output, but full open weights are not promised until July 27 — after this brief's window — so the open-source claim is currently unverifiable against real weights.
key_takeaways: Parameter count (2.8T) and context window (1M tokens) are the largest claimed for any model billed as open-weight, but the weights themselves are not out yet — treat the 'open' framing as provisional until July 27.
API pricing ($3/$0.30/$15 per M tokens) is already live and usable for evaluation independent of the weights release.
Kimi Delta Attention architecture is a genuinely new mechanism, not an incremental tune of a prior Kimi release.
top_picks.competitive_context: Directly challenges DeepSeek and Llama as the reference open-weight frontier model; if the July 27 weights release holds, it would be the largest open-weight model available for self-hosting, a relevant option for regulated enterprises wanting data-residency control over frontier-class capability.
top_picks.pricing: $3.00/M input tokens (cache miss), $0.30/M (cache hit), $15.00/M output tokens via Kimi API.

top_picks.title: Fireworks AI Raises $1.505B Series D at $17.5B Valuation
top_picks.summary: Fireworks AI closed a $1.505B Series D at a $17.5B post-money valuation, led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures, and TCV, with Nvidia, Lightspeed, Bessemer, Menlo, and others participating. The company's annualized revenue passed $1B, a roughly 5x year-over-year increase, and the valuation is roughly 4x its prior mark from about seven months earlier.
key_takeaways: 4x valuation increase in ~7 months signals investor conviction that custom/specialized model serving is a durable category, not just a frontier-API arbitrage play.
Customer base (Uber, Shopify per Fireworks' own materials) shows real enterprise production usage, not just developer-tier adoption.
Worth benchmarking against direct-API costs for any team running high-volume inference on open-weight models.
top_picks.competitive_context: Competes with Together AI, Baseten, and hyperscaler-native inference (AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry) for enterprises seeking cheaper alternatives to frontier-lab APIs; Nvidia's participation continues a pattern of the chipmaker investing directly in its largest inference customers.
top_picks.pricing: Not disclosed as part of the funding announcement.

top_picks.title: Claude Cowork Expands From Desktop-Only to iPhone, Android, and Web
top_picks.summary: Anthropic is expanding Claude Cowork, its background-agent feature, from the desktop app to iPhone, iPad, Android, and claude.ai. The rollout is a beta starting with the Max plan, with more plans to follow over several weeks; scheduled tasks now run with no device online, and Anthropic is extending its doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5 to cover the transition.
key_takeaways: Cross-device task handoff (start at desk, check on phone, review before shipping) is a meaningful workflow change for knowledge workers who use Claude for multi-step tasks.
Approval gating is preserved: Anthropic states nothing ships until a human reviews it, relevant for any team piloting this under existing AI-use policies.
Beta gated to Max plan first — broader plan availability timeline is not yet fixed, so budget for a phased pilot rather than org-wide rollout.
top_picks.competitive_context: Matches the general industry direction of persistent, cross-device background agents seen in OpenAI's and Google's own agent products; Anthropic's differentiation is the explicit human-approval checkpoint before any output ships.
top_picks.pricing: No new cost; included in existing paid Claude plans during beta, starting with Max.

top_picks.title: xAI Open-Sources Grok Build Codebase After Privacy Scandal
top_picks.summary: xAI published the roughly 844,530-line Rust codebase behind Grok Build on GitHub under an Apache 2.0 license, days after disclosures that the coding-agent product had been uploading users' private repository contents without adequate disclosure. Open-sourcing the codebase is presented as a transparency response to the incident.
key_takeaways: The open-sourcing follows a privacy incident, not a proactive strategy shift — treat the trust rebuild as unproven until independent audits confirm no residual data-handling issues.
Apache 2.0 licensing allows commercial forks and internal deployment, relevant if evaluating a self-hosted coding-agent stack.
Any prior enterprise pilot of Grok Build should re-review data-handling terms given the incident that prompted this release.
top_picks.competitive_context: Contrasts with closed coding-agent competitors (Cursor, GitHub Copilot); the incident itself is a cautionary data point for procurement teams evaluating any AI coding tool's repo-access permissions.
top_picks.pricing: Free and open source (Apache 2.0); underlying Grok model API usage still billed separately.

top_picks.title: InstaLILY Raises $60M Series B With Home Depot Ventures and United Rentals
top_picks.summary: InstaLILY, which builds AI 'teammates' that automate business-specific workflows for physical-goods distributors and field-service organizations, raised a $60M Series B led by Energize Capital. Insight Partners increased its existing investment, and Home Depot Ventures and United Rentals joined as new strategic investors, bringing total funding to nearly $100M following a year of 5x revenue growth.
key_takeaways: Strategic investors (Home Depot Ventures, United Rentals) are direct customers in building-products distribution and equipment rental, a strong signal this vendor's use cases map to industrial/building-materials workflows.
5x revenue growth in the prior year suggests real production deployment, not just pilot activity, among physical-goods distributors.
Worth a direct vendor briefing given the overlap between InstaLILY's target customer profile and enterprise building-products distribution operations.
top_picks.competitive_context: Competes in the emerging 'AI teammate for vertical operations' category alongside Sierra and Decagon, but InstaLILY's specific focus on distributors and field service differentiates it from more general customer-support-oriented agent vendors.

top_picks.title: xAI Launches Grok Automations for Scheduled and Email-Triggered Agent Tasks
top_picks.summary: xAI launched Grok Automations, letting users describe a task once and run it on a schedule (daily, weekday, weekly, monthly, yearly) or trigger it from matching incoming emails. Available now on grok.com and the Grok app for iOS and Android; scheduled automations are free for all users, while email-triggered automations require a SuperGrok subscription. Grok can connect to Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Outlook, GitHub, Linear, Notion, Vercel, and custom MCP connectors.
key_takeaways: MCP connector support means automations can be extended to internal tools without waiting for xAI to ship first-party integrations.
Email-trigger automations are gated behind SuperGrok, a real cost consideration for team-wide rollout versus per-user experimentation.
Positions Grok as a lightweight scheduled-agent layer competing directly with Zapier-plus-LLM stacks rather than just a chat interface.
top_picks.competitive_context: Directly comparable to OpenAI's scheduled tasks in ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude Cowork background agents launched the same week — three major labs converged on persistent/scheduled agent execution within days of each other.
top_picks.pricing: Scheduled automations free; email-triggered automations require SuperGrok subscription.
